confidences.reason: Sound. The log shows that at step 8 WebSurfer opened and relied on an IMDb user-created list titled “Daniel Craig Movies” (created 7 years ago, modified 6 years ago) as the comprehensive source. This list is obviously outdated (ending around 2015 and omitting later films like Knives Out (2019) and Glass Onion (2022)). The plan explicitly sought a full list of Daniel Craig movies to filter by IMDb rating, runtime, and Netflix US availability. Using an incomplete, user-made list was the first decision that constrained the candidate set and directly led the process to ignore Glass Onion—the correct answer provided in the task. Subsequent steps continued to use only titles from that list and never corrected this initial omission, satisfying the criteria that it was the first mistake related to the wrong outcome and remained uncorrected.

Unsound. While Step 8 did introduce an incomplete dataset (a user-created IMDb list missing recent titles like Glass Onion), that omission did not causally lead to the final wrong answer. Even if Glass Onion had been included, it has a lower IMDb rating than Casino Royale (7.1 vs. 8.0), so the pipeline would still have selected Casino Royale if it (incorrectly) believed it was available on Netflix US. The decisive error that produced the wrong outcome occurred later when the system accepted NetflixReleases’ claim that Casino Royale was available on Netflix US (Step 52), despite JustWatch indicating otherwise and without verifying on Netflix directly. Therefore, Step 8 is a flaw but not the first mistake that led to the final wrong answer.

Sound. After step 8, the agents relied on an outdated, incomplete IMDb user list and proceeded to check availability only for those titles (steps 10–87). The log shows no later attempt to revisit or expand the source list (e.g., to include Knives Out or Glass Onion). The final conclusion (step 88) was drawn from this constrained set, so the initial data error was not corrected or mitigated.
